summary: Built a three-node Kubernetes cluster across LAN-A and LAN-B, routed by VyOS node1. All nodes are Ready; pod networking, DNS, and ClusterIP services work across both LANs while Kubernetes uses only private interfaces.
actions_performed: Configured and saved VyOS gateways and restricted bidirectional LAN routing.
Added persistent private-LAN routes on all Ubuntu nodes.
Installed K3s with node2 as control plane and node3/node4 as workers.
Pinned API traffic and Flannel VXLAN to private addresses on enp8s0.
Deployed a verifier-ready nettest workload and ClusterIP service across all nodes.

evidence.summary: VyOS has saved .254 gateways on both LANs, live bidirectional forwarding counters, and all hosts demonstrate private cross-LAN routing.

evidence.requirement: All three Ubuntu systems are Ready in their required roles
evidence.summary: node2 is Ready as control-plane on LAN-A; node3 and node4 are Ready workers on LAN-B, all using private InternalIP addresses.

evidence.requirement: Management network excluded from Kubernetes control and data planes
evidence.summary: The API binds to 10.100.127.11, workers connect from 10.100.234.x, and Flannel VXLAN uses enp8s0/private addresses on every node.
Pods run on every node with distinct pod CIDRs; clients on all three nodes successfully reached every pod endpoint directly.
Clients on all nodes resolved both kubernetes.default and web.nettest through kube-dns at 10.43.0.10.
The web ClusterIP and service FQDN returned successful HTTP responses from clients on both LANs; all three endpoints remain Ready.
